keyVerseText: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people; a multitude: Heb. an assembly of people
rootMeaning: The root of קָהָל (qâhâl) is קָהַל (qâhal), which means to assemble or gather together, either for religious, political, or military purposes. This root conveys a sense of deliberate convocation, emphasizing the intentional coming together of people as an organized group. Unlike the general English term 'multitude,' the Hebrew root highlights the purposeful gathering or summoning of individuals into a unified assembly.
usageInScripture: The word קָהָל appears 123 times in Scripture and is most commonly translated as 'assembly,' 'congregation,' or 'company.' Its usage spans various contexts, including religious gatherings, civil affairs, and even war councils, reflecting its broad application to any organized body of people. The frequent translations such as 'and all the congregation' and 'the congregation' reveal a consistent emphasis on the collective nature of God's people, whether in worship, decision-making, or communal identity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קָהָל as a divinely appointed assembly enriches our appreciation of the church and Israel as communities called together by God’s sovereign will. This term underscores the importance of corporate identity and unity in the life of faith, reminding believers that they are not isolated individuals but part of a gathered people. It also points to the spiritual reality that God's purposes are fulfilled through the collective obedience and worship of His people. Christ, as the head of the church, summons His followers into this sacred assembly, continuing the biblical theme of a called-out congregation.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 28:3 blesses Jacob with fruitfulness and multiplication into 'a multitude of people,' literally 'an assembly of people' (קָהָל). This usage highlights God's intention for Jacob's descendants to be a distinct, organized community chosen for His purposes. The word קָהָל here enriches the verse by portraying this blessing not just as numerical increase but as the formation of a covenant community, called and gathered by God to fulfill His promises.
